Hi @spinler@us.ibm.com,

Thank you for tagging me to review this change.

**Regarding your concern about line 347 and the empty object path on line 434:**

You're right to point this out. If the condition on line 347 is never true (i.e., the button press duration doesn't exceed any of the configured thresholds), then `objPathName` will remain empty, which would cause a failure at line 434. As you mentioned, this issue existed before this change, but it's worth addressing.

I think we can fix this by modifying line 356 to check if `objPathName` has been set. If it hasn't, we should allow the code to fall through to the existing fallback logic below instead of breaking out of the switch case:

```
if (!objPathName.empty())
{
    break;
}
// If objPathName is still empty, continue to fallback logic
```
This way, if no multi-action threshold is matched, the system will gracefully fall back to the default power button behavior.

### Additional issues I found while reviewing this change:

### 1.Line 353 (the inner break statement): 
This break should be removed because multiPwrBtnActConf may contain multiple power policies with increasing duration thresholds. The current code will always apply the first matching policy and never reach longer-duration policies. We should continue iterating to find the best matching threshold.

### 2.Line 315 (hostNumStr format issue): 
In our multi-button configuration, getHostNumStr() returns "01", which creates an invalid path like "/xyz/openbmc_project/state/chassis01" instead of the correct "/xyz/openbmc_project/state/chassis1".

Here's our D-Bus tree for reference:
```
root@bmc:~# busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Chassis.Buttons
└─ /xyz
  └─ /xyz/openbmc_project
    └─ /xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis
      └─ /xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis/Buttons
        ├─ /xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis/Buttons/Power01
        ├─ /xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis/Buttons/Power02
        ...
```
### 3.Line 345 (vector indexing): 
I agree that multiPwrBtnActConf[stoi(hostNumStr) - 1] could cause problems. I believe the multi-action feature is not exclusively for multi-button scenarios; it should also work for a single button. The purpose of multi-action is to support multiple power policies (based on press duration) for any given button. Therefore, I have some ideas to strengthen how multiPwrBtnActConf is captured and applied.I've prepared a patch addressing these issues that might be helpful: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-buttons/+/85636

I'd appreciate your thoughts and feedback on this approach.

Thanks, Liora

Hi @patrick@stwcx.xyz,

Thanks for calling this out — let me clarify where the "01" is coming from.

You’re right that if getHostNumStr() is viewed in isolation, the use of
substr(len - 1) suggests that only a single character would be returned.
That’s also why this behavior is not obvious from that function alone.

The key detail is how the DBus object path is constructed.
`POWER_DBUS_OBJECT_NAME` is defined as:
```
  "/xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis/Buttons/Power0"
```
In button_factory, for multi-instance buttons, the object path is built as:
```
  getDbusObjectPath() + indexStr
```
As a result, the actual DBus objects created are, for example:
```
  root@bmc:~# busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Chassis.Buttons
  └─ /xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis/Buttons/Power01
  └─ /xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis/Buttons/Power02
  ...
```
Given these zero-padded object names, the substring logic in getHostNumStr()
can return values like "01" rather than just "1". This is the concern I was
raising, as it can lead to constructing an invalid chassis state path and
cause the multi FIO power button to have no effect.

To be clear, this is not an issue with getHostNumStr() in isolation, but with
the interaction between DBus object path construction and its parsing.

I think addressing this before merging would help avoid regressing multi FIO
button behavior.

I think there are two ways to fix this.
A) modify getHostNumStr(), let it return string depend on isMultiHost().
B) modify  void addToRegistry(size_t index) let DBus Obj like following:
```
  root@bmc:~# busctl tree xyz.openbmc_project.Chassis.Buttons
  └─ /xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis/Buttons/Power1
  └─ /xyz/openbmc_project/Chassis/Buttons/Power2
```
B-way:  This is better but I can't verify this on my platform.

Hi @spinler@us.ibm.com,

Thanks again for the review and for looping me in.

I still have one concern from my earlier comment (Patchset 5, Nov 30). In the multi-button case, getHostNumStr() returns "01". When we build:

    objPathName = CHASSIS_STATE_OBJECT_NAME + hostNumStr;

the chassis state object path becomes `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/chassis01`. The chassis state object provided by phosphor-state-manager is `/xyz/openbmc_project/state/chassis1`, so the resulting path is invalid. Because of that, the power control cannot be executed and the FIO power button ends up having no effect.

I’m planning to help address this issue in a follow-up patch, but I wanted to make sure we’re aligned on the problem before this change is merged.



Thanks,
Liora
